name: Desmin-related myopathy with Mallory body-like inclusions

criteria.description: Progressive skeletal muscle weakness predominantly affecting proximal muscles
Presence of Mallory body-like cytoplasmic inclusions in muscle biopsy
Identification of pathogenic DES gene mutation
Evidence of cardiomyopathy or conduction defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness, Mallory body-like inclusions on muscle biopsy, and pathogenic DES gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac evaluation is recommended due to frequent cardiac involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mallory body-like cytoplasmic inclusions in muscle fibers

searchTerms: gradual shoulder and hip muscle weakness
heart muscle disease with rhythm problems

common.symptomName: Muscle atrophy predominantly in limb girdle muscles
searchTerms: muscle wasting around shoulders and hips
loss of muscle bulk in limb girdle
muscle disease changes on EMG test

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness
irregular heart rhythms including AV block
mild weakness in hands and feet

rare.symptomName: Dysphagia due to pharyngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to muscle involvement

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty replacement and atrophy of proximal muscles
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating Mallory body-like eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions
Electromyography showing myopathic motor unit potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Broader spectrum of protein aggregates beyond desmin inclusions
Variable genetic causes including other sarcomeric proteins
Absence of Mallory body-like inclusions on muscle biopsy
Different genetic mutations and inheritance patterns

redFlags: Rapid progression of muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Presence of Mallory body-like inclusions on muscle biopsy
references: Schröder R, et al. Desmin-related myopathy with Mallory body-like inclusions: clinical and pathological features. Neurology. 2003.
Orphanet: Desmin-related myopathy with Mallory body-like inclusions. ORPHA:84132.
Clemen CS, et al. Desminopathies: pathology and mechanisms. Acta Neuropathol. 2013.
